questions.question: Explain the difference between a wage and a salary in terms of the unit being sold, and how each is read from a scale or a rate.
questions.expected_answer: A wage sells the hour: pay equals hours worked times an hourly rate, so gross responds to the week and lands weekly or fortnightly. A salary sells the year: one fixed annual amount for a position, paid in twelve equal monthly slices regardless of the month's workload. The salary is governed by a scale read as start × annual increment — ceiling; the wage is governed by an hourly rate plus contracted overtime multipliers.

questions.question: Run Ndlovu's week (40 normal hours at R50, 3 evening overtime hours) and Adams's week (40 normal hours at R44, 2 Sunday hours) to gross, showing the labelled lines the working demands.
questions.expected_answer: Ndlovu: normal 40 × 50 = R2 000; overtime rate at time and a half = R75; overtime 3 × 75 = R225; gross R2 225. Adams: normal 40 × 44 = R1 760; Sunday rate at double time = R88; Sunday pay 2 × 88 = R176; gross R1 936. Each overtime rate is derived as its own labelled line before the hours are touched; the week's wage bill is R4 161.

questions.question: The administrator is in her second year on the scale R120 000 × R12 000 — R180 000. State her current monthly salary, and calculate when she reaches the ceiling.
questions.expected_answer: One completed year of service moved her one notch, from R120 000 to R132 000 per year — R11 000 per month. The scale's distance is R60 000; divided by the R12 000 notch that is five increments, so the ceiling of R180 000 is reached at the start of her sixth year of service.
